final_prompt:
Please write a polite email to my landlord about the late fee. Cite the lease section. Thank you!

<document>
From: Dana Whitfield, Maple Court Apartments
Subject: Late fee - Unit 3B

Hi,

Our records show this month's rent was received on the 3rd. As you know, rent is due
on the 1st, so a late fee of $75 has been added to your account. We were disappointed
to see this, since on-time payments help us keep the building running for everyone.
We'd appreciate it if you could be more careful going forward. Please pay the fee
along with next month's rent.

Thanks for understanding,
Dana

---
Lease excerpt (Maple Court residential lease):
Section 4.1: Rent is $1,450 per month, payable by check, money order, or the resident
portal.
Section 4.2: Rent is due on the 1st. A grace period applies through the 5th; no late
fees may be charged during the grace period.
Section 4.3: Returned payments incur a $35 fee.
Section 9.4: Notices to the landlord must be in writing and may be sent by email.
</document>

Here's a polite email you can send to Dana:

**Subject:** Late fee on Unit 3B – question regarding Section 4.2

Hi Dana,

Thank you for letting me know about the late fee on my account for this month. I wanted to check it against the lease, and I believe the fee may not apply.

Section 4.2 of the Maple Court residential lease states that rent is due on the 1st, with a grace period through the 5th, and that no late fees may be charged during the grace period. My payment was received on the 3rd, which falls within that grace period, so I'd ask that the $75 late fee be reversed.

I'm happy to look at the payment records together if that would help. Thank you for your attention to this, and I look forward to your reply.

Best regards,
[Your name]
Unit 3B

---

Before sending, you may want to confirm that the payment was received on the 3rd and not later, and keep a copy of this email for your records. Since Section 9.4 allows notices by email, this message is a valid written notice.
